brief.headline: Aluminium snapped a five-session slide with its biggest one-day gain of the month - but every base metal rose on the same falling dollar, and aluminium's own front end got LOOSER while it happened, so this reads as a currency move rather than a shortage.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: the London three-month benchmark settled $3,244/t on 21-August, up 1.92%, and cash $3,227/t, up 1.41% - the largest single-day gain of the month and the first higher close in six sessions. That trims the give-back from the 11-August high to 4.3% and lifts the year-to-date gain back to +7.8%.

WHY IT MOVED - AND WHY THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE MOVE: all five exchange base metals rose together (zinc +2.2%, aluminium +1.9%, copper +1.9%, nickel +1.0%, lead +0.6%), gold rose for a fifth straight week, and the dollar fell about 0.8% on the week to its lowest since May. When everything priced in dollars goes up at once, the dollar is usually the story. A rally you can explain without mentioning aluminium tells you little about aluminium.

THE PART THAT DID NOT IMPROVE: the discount between metal for immediate delivery and metal in three months WIDENED from $1 to $17 - a fourth straight session in which the market declined to pay extra for metal it can have today - and exchange warehouse stocks were unchanged for a FOURTH consecutive session at 246,925 tonnes, neither building nor drawing. Price and market structure moved in opposite directions for the second day running. Zinc offers the contrast: it got the same dollar push and its front end TIGHTENED while its stocks fell.

WHAT TO WATCH: the US regional premium - the extra buyers pay above the exchange price - fell 8.2% in a single session to about $2,094/t on reports Washington will halve tariffs on Canadian metal, with later months down more than 12%. No proclamation has been published and the legal rate is still 50%, which means roughly 77% of that premium is now policy rather than physical scarcity. Watch for the actual legal text, and watch whether the flat stock line finally breaks in either direction.

kpis.label: LME Cash settlement
kpis.note: SATURDAY-COMPILED FOR 22-AUGUST ON THE FRIDAY 21-AUGUST OFFICIAL BOARD, WHICH IS THE LATEST PUBLISHED SETTLEMENT AND A GENUINELY NEW SESSION RATHER THAN A CARRIED ONE. THE CACHE CROSS-CHECK CAME BACK CLEAN FOR A TENTH CONSECUTIVE RUN: the cache-busted GERMAN overview and the cache-busted ENGLISH overview returned the identical 21-August board, with all six metals, all six stock lines and all three FX fixings rolling together (EUR/USD LME-FX 1.17010 against 1.16860 on 20-August, ECB fixing 1.16990 against 1.16810, BFIX 1.16996 against 1.16846). A THIRD, STRONGER CHECK WAS ADDED THIS RUN AND IT ALSO PASSED: the August month-to-date cash averages computed independently from the fifteen individual published sessions on this board reconcile EXACTLY to Westmetall's own monthly-averages pages - aluminium $3,261.80, zinc $3,816.43 and lead $1,850.23 all match to the cent. That is a far harder test than comparing two renderings of the same page, because it can only pass if every individual session in the window is correct. Ten clean fetches now stand against four logged cache incidents earlier in the cycle (31-Jul per-metal tables, 04-Aug English overview, 11-Aug per-metal tables, 12-Aug English overview). THE FIVE-SESSION SLIDE ENDED WITH THE LARGEST SINGLE-DAY GAIN OF THE MONTH - AND THE FRONT END LOOSENED WHILE IT HAPPENED. Cash settled $3,227.00, UP $45.00 (+1.41%) from $3,182.00. The three-month settled $3,244.00, UP $61.00 (+1.92%). FOR THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE SESSION THE SPREAD AND THE FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, AND THAT IS CALLED OUT EXPLICITLY BECAUSE THE POLARITY HAS NOW REVERSED: on 20-August the price fell while the curve tightened; on 21-August the price ROSE while the curve LOOSENED. The cash-3M discount WIDENED from a $1.00 contango to a $17.00 contango - the fourth consecutive contango and, at $17.00, the second-widest of the four. YESTERDAY THIS DASHBOARD PUBLISHED A BINARY TEST IN ADVANCE AND THE HONEST SCORING IS THAT ONE LIMB RESOLVED AND ONE LIMB DID NOT RESOLVE AT ALL. THE SPREAD LIMB RESOLVED FOR THE BEARS, CLEANLY: the test asked whether a fourth contango would print and whether it would re-widen. It did both. The escalation path this board warned about on 20-August and which failed to appear that session appeared on this one. THE INVENTORY LIMB DID NOT RESOLVE: the test asked for an outright BUILD or a RESUMED DRAW and got NEITHER. LME aluminium stock was UNCHANGED at 246,925 tonnes for a FOURTH consecutive session - a reported daily change of exactly ZERO on 18, 19, 20 and 21-August. A test that specifies two outcomes and gets a third is a test that was mis-specified, and that is stated rather than scored generously. FOUR FLAT PRINTS ARE NOW THEIR OWN SIGNAL: the run of 34 consecutive daily declines that ended on 18-August has been switched off for a full trading week, and a warrant line that neither builds nor draws for four sessions is describing metal that is neither being warranted nor cancelled - stasis, not scarcity. THE GAIN CANNOT BE ATTRIBUTED TO ALUMINIUM, AND THAT IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT QUALIFICATION ON THIS BOARD. ALL FIVE BASE METALS ROSE on the 21-August official - zinc +2.16%, aluminium +1.92%, copper +1.89%, nickel +0.98%, lead +0.64% - which is a complex-wide move, not a metal-specific one. The LME EUR/USD fixing rose again to 1.17010 from 1.16860, the dollar index fell about 0.79% on the week to its lowest since May, and the London gold fix jumped to $4,581.95 from $4,487.60, a 2.10% single-session gain and a fifth consecutive weekly advance. A dollar-denominated commodity that rises 1.92% into a falling dollar alongside every one of its exchange peers and a bid gold price is being repriced by the numeraire, not by its own fundamentals. THE STRUCTURE AGREES WITH THAT READING: if this were prompt scarcity the front end would have tightened. It loosened. THE GIVE-BACK FROM THE 11-AUGUST HIGH OF $3,373.00 NARROWS TO $146.00 (-4.33%) IN EIGHT SESSIONS, and the market now holds $67.50 (+2.14%) above the 28-July swing low of $3,159.50 carried here as the explicit technical invalidation - a cushion three times wider than the $22.50 recorded yesterday. The August cash average-to-date on the published averages page is $3,261.80 across fifteen sessions, so today's settlement sits $34.80 BELOW the month's own mean: the back half of August is still undoing the front half, just less of it than it was.

kpis.label: LME 3-Month
kpis.note: The 21-August official three-month settled $3,244.00, UP $61.00 (+1.92%) from $3,183.00 - the largest single-session gain on the forward since 10-August and the move that ended a five-session decline. It sits $17.00 ABOVE cash, which is a CONTANGO by the convention stated on this board - cash below three-month - and it is the FOURTH consecutive one. THE MECHANICAL POINT IS THE WHOLE POINT TODAY: the forward rose $61.00 while the prompt rose only $45.00, so the forward outran the prompt by $16.00 and that difference IS the widening of the discount. Read against the previous session this is a clean reversal of roles - on 20-August the forward fell three times harder than the prompt and closed the contango; on 21-August the forward rose harder than the prompt and reopened it. In both cases the FORWARD is doing the work and the prompt is following, which is the signature of a curve being moved by macro positioning at the liquid tenor rather than by physical availability at the front. Year-to-date the three-month is +7.76% against the first-published 2026 official of $3,010.50 on 02-January, recovered from +5.73% yesterday but still well below the 2026 peak of +12.07% on 11-August; a little over a third of the lost year-to-date gain has been won back in one session. Read against the 11-August cycle high of $3,374.00 on the same tenor, the forward has surrendered $130.00 (-3.85%) in eight sessions, against cash's $146.00 (-4.33%) - the two tenors have DIVERGED again after converging on 20-August, which is the arithmetic of a curve tipping back into contango. The August three-month average-to-date on the published averages page is $3,259.13, so the forward closed $15.13 BELOW its own monthly mean.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: MINUS $17.00 - A FOURTH CONSECUTIVE CONTANGO, AND IT RE-WIDENED SEVENTEENFOLD. Cash $3,227.00 settled $17.00 BELOW the three-month of $3,244.00, against a $1.00 contango on 20-August, $20.50 on 19-August and $15.00 on 18-August, which had itself crossed from exactly $0.00 on 17-August. The sequence now reads 0.00, -15.00, -20.50, -1.00, -17.00. CONVENTION, STATED EVERY RUN SO IT CANNOT BE MISREAD: cash ABOVE three-month is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt scarcity; cash BELOW three-month is CONTANGO and signals the market will not pay for prompt metal. THE SPREAD AND THE FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS FOR A SECOND CONSECUTIVE SESSION WITH THE POLARITY REVERSED, AND THIS IS WHERE THE USEFUL INFORMATION SITS. A market that rallies 1.92% on the forward while its front end loosens by $16.00 is not discovering scarcity; it is being lifted. The contrast with 20-August is instructive precisely because it is exact: that session fell on the price and tightened on the structure, which is a market repricing the LEVEL while availability held; this session rose on the price and loosened on the structure, which is a market repricing the LEVEL again, in the other direction, while availability continued to deteriorate. In both readings the structure is the quieter and more consistent signal, and the structure has now printed at or below parity on FIVE consecutive official settlements. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS READ. A return to outright backwardation while the flat price holds would be the first genuine evidence since 11-August that prompt metal is being competed for. Nothing on this board shows that. The July average spread was a $7.05 BACKWARDATION on the published monthly averages, so the front end remains materially looser than its own recent norm and moved further away from it on this session.

drivers.text: A REPORTED US-CANADA TARIFF FRAMEWORK TOOK 8.2% OUT OF THE US MIDWEST PREMIUM IN ONE SESSION - THE RISK CONVERTED INTO A PRICE — This board has carried a US-Canada tariff agreement as a named risk to the US duty-paid premium for several runs. On 20-August it stopped being a risk and became an assessment: the September Midwest transaction premium was assessed at 95.0 cents/lb, about $2,094/t, DOWN 8.2% on the day, with October and November contracts down more than 12%, on reporting that Washington is set to halve the Section 232 rate on Canadian steel and aluminium from 50% to 25%. Canada supplies more than half of United States aluminium imports, so the pass-through is direct and mechanical. TWO QUALIFICATIONS ARE PUBLISHED ALONGSIDE IT. First, NO PROCLAMATION OR FEDERAL REGISTER NOTICE HAS BEEN ISSUED - the terms are reported as unfinished, derivative products may carry different rates, and the published rate remains 50%; the physical market has repriced an expectation, not a law. Second, Morgan Stanley's published view is that Canada cannot supply all US demand even at a lower rate, so residual tonnes still entering at 50% put a floor under how far the premium can fall. The deeper falls in the October and November contracts than in September say the market expects the change to bite with a lag.
drivers.source: Bloomberg via Mining.com - Aluminum premium slips as US set to cut tariffs on Canada metal (20-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: A FRAMING CORRECTION IS MADE OPENLY THIS RUN: THE 15% SECTION 232 RATE IS NOT A PRIMARY-METAL CARVE-OUT — This board has previously described a 15% Annex I-C rate for Japan, Korea, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Taiwan and EU member states in a way that could be read as applying to primary aluminium. IT DOES NOT, AND THE CORRECTION IS STATED RATHER THAN QUIETLY AMENDED. Under the 02-April-2026 proclamation effective 06-April, ANNEX I-A APPLIES 50% TO ARTICLES MADE ENTIRELY OR ALMOST ENTIRELY OF ALUMINIUM - generally HTSUS Chapter 76, which is where P1020 primary metal sits - and Annex I-B applies 25% to derivative articles that are not almost entirely aluminium. The 01-June-2026 proclamation effective 08-June created ANNEX I-C, which covers MOBILE INDUSTRIAL EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY ONLY; its rates are 25% generally, 10% where metal content is entirely US-origin, and 15% for a named list that does include Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and EU members, calibrated so that MFN Column 1 plus Section 232 totals 15%. PRIMARY ALUMINIUM FROM EVERY ONE OF THOSE COUNTRIES STILL PAYS 50%. Other verified structural features: tariffs now apply to FULL CUSTOMS VALUE rather than metal content; steel, aluminium and copper 232 tariffs do not stack; a 10% rate applies where metal was smelted and cast in the US; the UK pays 25% in place of 50%; and Russian-origin primary metal carries 200%.
drivers.source: The White House - Strengthening Actions Taken to Adjust Imports of Aluminum, Steel, and Copper (02-Apr-2026)

drivers.text: THE HORMUZ CONSTRAINT HARDENED ON A DATED OFFICIAL ADVISORY - CARGO TRANSITS WERE LITERALLY ZERO ON THREE CONSECUTIVE DAYS — The single largest structural support under Asian and Gulf-linked premiums escalated on public, official, dated evidence this run rather than merely persisting. The UKMTO/JMIC Advisory Update 086 dated 18-August-2026 places the JMIC threat level at SEVERE, stating that deliberate hostile action is considered highly likely, and records CARGO VESSEL TRANSITS OF ZERO ON 15, 16 AND 17 AUGUST against a 2025 baseline of roughly 138 vessels per day, with tanker transits of zero, zero and three. It logs 91 confirmed vessel incidents since 01-March-2026, persistent GPS jamming and spoofing, and active drifting-mine risk. Reporting also indicates the 17-June-2026 US-Iran memorandum lapsed around 16-August. The aluminium-specific consequence is reported rather than asserted: Kpler-sourced coverage describes Gulf smelters having lost direct seaborne alumina and bauxite access since early March and now transhipping via an anchorage in north-west India onto geared vessels for Fujairah, a routing described as neither efficient nor sustainable, and unsafe for alumina powder in monsoon conditions.

ASIAN SPOT PREMIUMS ARE DRIFTING LOWER INTO THE Q4 MJP ROUND, WHICH IS WHY Q4 IS PUBLISHED AS A RANGE AND NOT A NUMBER — The Q4-2026 Main Japanese Port negotiation conventionally opens in early September and settles mid-to-late September, against a Q3 settlement of $395/t that is the highest in about a decade. NOTHING PUBLIC HAS PRINTED INSIDE THAT ROUND - no settlement, no offer range, no first-deal report - so this board publishes a scenario range of $305-395/t and explicitly not an assessment. The publicly available inputs point in conflicting directions and both are carried. AGAINST SELLERS: SMM's 11-August overseas premium review reports Japanese spot premiums continuing to move lower with cargoes hard to sell and buyers holding bargaining power; the LME front end has now printed at or below parity on five consecutive official settlements, removing the backwardation exhibit sellers normally lead with; and market commentary expects Q4 to ease as Middle East flows normalise. FOR SELLERS: the Gulf supply constraint documented above is unresolved and hardened this week, and Chinese physical ingot inventory has continued to destock. NO NUMBER IS TAKEN FROM ANY OF THIS.
drivers.source: SMM via AL Circle - Asian primary aluminium spot premiums remain weak (11-Aug-2026)

prices.note: THE ONE CLEAN, FREE, DATED, SETTLED ALUMINA PRICE ON THIS PAGE, AND THE FIRST TO MOVE MEANINGFULLY IN THIS CYCLE. LME Alumina closed $363.20/t on 20-August, UP 2.23% on the day from $355.26 on 19-August, and up 5.3% from $344.79/t on 11-August - a sustained seven-session advance on a settled series rather than an assessment. This is a cost-push signal for non-integrated smelters and it is the reason the alumina risk on this board was moved this run from a decaying threat to a stable one. THE RATIO IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS AND IT REMAINS COMFORTABLE: at $363.20/t against an aluminium three-month of $3,244.00 the alumina-to-aluminium ratio is 11.2% against a decade norm of 15-17%, so alumina is still historically cheap relative to metal and the smelter margin cushion is wide. A CONFIGURATION IMPROVEMENT IS WORTH NOTING: for several compiles the ratio drifted up because the METAL was falling, which erodes margin from the revenue side; on this board metal rose 1.92% and alumina 2.23%, so both legs moved up together and the ratio is roughly stable. prices.note: THE CHINESE INDEX IS DRIFTING LOWER WHILE EX-CHINA STRENGTHENS, AND THAT DIVERGENCE IS THE MOST INFORMATIVE ALUMINA READ ON THIS BOARD. SMM's Alumina Weekly Review dated 20-August-2026 marks the China index at RMB 2,681.62/mt, DOWN RMB 8.73 week-on-week, and is headlined explicitly that the spread between Chinese and overseas markets is widening. THE ARITHMETIC OF THE GAP: FOB Western Australia at $360/mt with freight at $32/mt implies a China main-port equivalent of about RMB 3,066.17/mt - roughly RMB 385/mt ABOVE the domestic index. Seven ex-China spot trades cleared in the week, including $409/mt CIF Rotterdam and $400/mt FOB Jamaica, both on 14-August. SUPPLY IS NOT THE CONSTRAINT AND THAT IS STATED SO THE DIVERGENCE IS NOT OVER-READ: China's alumina operating rate was flat week-on-week at 74.33%, on 88.01 Mt/y operating against 118.42 Mt/y installed - very substantial idle capacity - and total Chinese alumina inventory fell only 30,000 mt to 7.245 Mt. SMM attributes the ex-China strength to Middle East transport problems lifting bagged-alumina demand and to tight Indonesian bauxite, which makes this a cost of war rather than a cost of production. Source: https://news.metal.com/en/newscontent/104071034-alumina-in-china-drifts-lower-outside-china-continues-to-strengthen-and-the-price-spread-between-chinese-and-overseas-ma

It logs 91 confirmed vessel incidents since 01-March-2026, persistent GPS jamming and spoofing, and active drifting-mine risk; a separate UKMTO advisory records a general cargo ship struck by a projectile half a nautical mile off Oman with one crew fatality. Reporting indicates the 17-June-2026 US-Iran memorandum lapsed around 16-August and that diplomacy has stalled. Day 174 counted to today's report date. THE ALUMINIUM CONSEQUENCE IS REPORTED RATHER THAN ASSERTED: Kpler-sourced coverage describes Gulf smelters transhipping alumina and bauxite via a north-west India anchorage onto geared vessels for Fujairah then trucking inland, a routing described as neither efficient nor sustainable and unsafe for alumina powder in monsoon conditions. logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor

Lloyd's List's Red Sea Brief dated 20-August-2026 records Suez traffic at a TWO-YEAR HIGH, with 1,088-1,090 transits and 88.6 million deadweight tonnes in the four weeks to 16-August, the highest since January 2024 - though still roughly 41% below pre-crisis levels. JMIC assesses Bab al Mandeb and the southern Red Sea at SUBSTANTIAL and the northern Red Sea and Suez at MODERATE, with Suez operations normal. THE OFFSETS ARE CARRIED RATHER THAN DROPPED: the Houthis declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia specifically on 20-July and enforce it selectively, Al-Mokha port is closed after more than 25 missile impacts, and a Somali piracy resurgence has produced two vessel seizures in four days with five merchant vessels still held. For an aluminium board this corridor matters mainly for Asia-Europe semis and billet flows rather than for Gulf primary metal.

The LME's own EUR/USD LME-FX fixing on the 21-August board is 1.17010 against 1.16860 on 20-August; the ECB 14:15 fixing is 1.16990 against 1.16810; BFIX is 1.16996 against 1.16846. All three moved together and by a similar magnitude, which is one of the internal-consistency checks used to confirm this board is a genuinely new session rather than a cached snapshot - and this run added a harder check on top of it, reconciling the August month-to-date cash averages computed from the fifteen individual sessions to Westmetall's published monthly-averages pages, which matched exactly for aluminium, zinc and lead. A stronger euro mechanically lowers the local-currency cost of a dollar-priced import for European buyers and is a marginal support for European duty-unpaid demand, though not one that shows up inside a single day.

row.label: USD/CNY
row.note: USD/CNY marks 6.72041 with the yuan marginally stronger on the day; SMM used 6.74 in its 20-August alumina import-parity arithmetic. THIS ROW REPLACES THE YEN LINE THIS RUN BECAUSE THE YUAN IS WHERE THE ACTIVE ARBITRAGE SITS. SMM published a dated 21-August analysis stating that the SHFE-to-LME price ratio has recovered far enough that NET PRIMARY ALUMINIUM IMPORTS INTO CHINA SHOULD RISE and that semis export demand should weaken gradually as existing order books are digested. That matters directly to this board in both directions: more Chinese import demand is a bullish pull on ex-China units, while fading semis exports would eventually relieve the pressure China's export surge has been putting on Western markets - China's July unwrought aluminium and semis exports were 640,000 tonnes, up 18.7% year-on-year, with January to July at 4.04 million tonnes, up 16.7%. A recovering ratio is the mechanism by which those two flows swap places, and it is worth watching every run from here.

row.label: US 10-year Treasury yield
row.note: The US 10-year marks 4.737%, up 3.1 basis points on the day, with Trading Economics headlining that the yield is approaching a twenty-month high. THE POLICY REGIME IS THE PART THAT IS MOST OFTEN GOT WRONG AND IT IS STATED EXPLICITLY: this is a HIKING-RISK environment, not a cutting cycle. CME FedWatch pricing has September at 59.9% unchanged against 40.1% for a 25 basis point HIKE, and October at 45.3% unchanged, 44.9% for a hike and 9.8% for 50 basis points. Bloomberg's economist survey has the Fed on hold through to end-July 2027, with core PCE seen averaging 3.2% in 2026. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks at Jackson Hole on 27-29 August, his first as chair, which is a dated and material macro catalyst for every dollar-priced commodity on this board. FOR THE CURVE ITSELF THE YIELD MATTERS THROUGH FINANCING COST: contango carry trades only work when the spread exceeds financing plus storage, and a $17.00 contango on a $3,227 cash price with the ten-year near 4.74% is nowhere close to covering carry. headlines.title: LME aluminium ends a five-session slide with its largest one-day gain of the month: the 21-August official three-month settled $3,244.00, up $61.00 (+1.92%), and cash settled $3,227.00, up $45.00 (+1.41%). Trading Economics' benchmark tracker independently marks aluminium +1.91% on the day and SMM marks LME aluminium +1.79% overnight, so three separate series agree on the direction and roughly on the magnitude.

Every base metal on the board rose on the same session, which means aluminium's gain cannot be attributed to aluminium: zinc +2.16%, aluminium +1.92%, copper +1.89%, nickel +0.98% and lead +0.64% on the LME three-month, alongside gold +1.97% overnight for a fifth consecutive weekly gain and a dollar index down about 0.79% on the week to its lowest since May. This is tagged Mixed rather than Bullish precisely because a macro-driven rally carries less information about aluminium's own balance than a metal-specific one.

LME aluminium stock was unchanged at 246,925 tonnes for a FOURTH consecutive session on 21-August, and the cash-to-three-month discount re-widened from $1.00 to $17.00 - a fourth consecutive contango. Cancelled warrants remain only about 2,450 tonnes against 244,475 tonnes of live warrants, a cancellation ratio near 1%, which is not the profile of metal being pulled out of the system.

The US Midwest transaction premium fell 8.2% in a single session on 20-August to 95.0 cents/lb, about $2,094/t, with October and November contracts down more than 12%, after reporting that Washington is set to cut Section 232 tariffs on Canadian metal from 50% to 25%. Canada supplies more than half of US aluminium imports. This is the largest single move on the physical side of this board and it went the opposite way to the exchange price.

A US-Canada framework is reported to halve steel and aluminium tariffs to 25% and cut Canadian auto duties to 15%, with a scheduled escalation on other Canadian goods paused; no proclamation or Federal Register notice has been issued and terms are described as unfinished, with different rates possible on some derivatives. The administration is reported to be leaning on Section 338 of the 1930 Tariff Act following the February-2026 Supreme Court ruling that curbed the broader tariff authority.

US BIS has proposed adding 14 derivative article categories to the Section 232 aluminium, steel and copper scope, including aluminium powder, electric conductor cables, heat-exchanger parts, cranes and trailers, most at 25%; the comment period opened 04-August. Since 06-April-2026 Section 232 has applied 50% to the full customs value of primary metal articles and 25% to the full value of derivatives.

SMM's 21-August aluminium spot afternoon review records SHFE futures stabilising, good warehouse withdrawals in Wuxi, generally bullish supplier sentiment, East China A00 mainstream transactions back to a range of a RMB 10/mt discount to a RMB 10/mt premium, an East China procurement sentiment index up 0.07 to 3.23, and aluminium ingot inventory in major consumption areas DOWN 12,000 mt on the day with only one region building. A companion South China review the same morning is headlined that futures stopped falling and rebounded with large traders sharply raising prices.

Chinese aluminium BILLET inventory in major consumption areas reached 143,000 tonnes on 20-August, the highest for the period in five years, up 6,000 tonnes on the prior Thursday - and SMM states plainly that peak-season restocking has failed to materialise, with downstream operating rates under pressure. Ingot inventory continues to destock while billet builds, which is the clearest available evidence that the destock is a supply-side phenomenon rather than a demand-side one.

SMM reports the SHFE-to-LME price ratio has recovered enough that net primary aluminium imports into China should rise and semis export demand should weaken gradually as order books are digested. China's July unwrought aluminium and semis exports were 640,000 tonnes, up 18.7% year-on-year, with January-July at 4.04 million tonnes, up 16.7% - a surplus being exported as semis rather than ingot.

Alumina outside China is strengthening while Chinese alumina drifts lower and the spread widens: the SMM China index marked RMB 2,681.62/mt (down RMB 8.73 week-on-week) against FOB Western Australia at $360/mt, implying a China main-port equivalent about RMB 385/mt above the domestic index, with ex-China trades at $409/mt CIF Rotterdam and $400/mt FOB Jamaica. LME Alumina separately closed $363.20/t on 20-August, up 2.23% on the day and up 5.3% in seven sessions. Tagged bullish for the alumina line and therefore a cost headwind for non-integrated smelters.

The UKMTO/JMIC advisory dated 18-August places the Strait of Hormuz threat level at SEVERE, with cargo vessel transits of exactly zero on 15, 16 and 17 August against a 2025 baseline near 138 per day, 91 confirmed vessel incidents since 01-March, persistent GPS jamming and active drifting-mine risk. Gulf smelters are reported to be transhipping alumina via a north-west India anchorage onto geared vessels for Fujairah, a routing described as neither efficient nor sustainable.

The Gulf's largest smelter reports 227 reduction cells restarted as of 10-August, about 18% of total, with hot metal guided back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 on a repair programme of roughly US$408 million; its 2.4 Mt/y alumina refinery restarted 10-July and is guided to full technical capability by end-2026. Supply relief on a dated, published schedule is the dominant bearish structural item on this board.

China's NEV penetration topped 50% for the first time in July at 1.561 million units, up 23.7% year-on-year, but total July auto sales fell to about 2.584 million units, down 8% month-on-month, with domestic sales down 23.6% year-on-year and exports up 81.3%; SMM still expects full-year domestic NEV sales down more than 10% year-on-year. Aluminium intensity per vehicle is rising while the vehicle count is not.

Canada's H1-2026 aluminium exports to the United States fell 25.03% to 1,039,551 tonnes from 1.39 million tonnes in H1-2025, with total Canadian exports down about 2% as only roughly 42% of the lost US volume was re-routed elsewhere; the two-year decline in shipments to the US is about 35.97%. Displaced Canadian metal landing in Europe is a direct bearish input to European duty-paid premiums.

SMM published a 21-August analysis of an LME copper short squeeze - a squeeze, then ship-to-delivery-warehouse, then return cycle - noting the copper cash-to-three-month backwardation had briefly reached a roughly five-year high. If that is what has been unwinding, copper's four-session structural collapse from a $535 backwardation to $56 is a positioning event rather than a supply one, which materially weakens the copper-to-aluminium read-across this board has been drawing all week.

backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 38.0% directional hit rate against a 70.5% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 1.52% versus 7.04% after 'loosening' readings. earnings.note: SWUNG BACK TO PROFIT ON THE PRICE CYCLE, WITH TEXTBOOK OPERATING LEVERAGE. Unaudited H1-2026 interim results, approved at an 18-August board meeting and filed 19-August: ADJUSTED EBITDA UP 64.4% TO US$1.23bn from US$748m; revenue up 10.9% to US$8.338bn from US$7.52bn; adjusted net profit US$196m against a US$194m loss a year earlier. Total sales cost rose 3.3% to US$6.31bn, attributed to higher energy costs. REVENUE UP A TENTH AGAINST EBITDA UP NEARLY TWO-THIRDS IS THE SAME OPERATING-LEVERAGE SIGNATURE EVERY OTHER PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL HAS REPORTED FOR THE FIRST HALF, and it confirms the pattern extends beyond Western and Gulf smelters. The cost line is the part worth noting rather than the profit line: sales cost rose only 3.3% while revenue rose 10.9%, so the margin expansion came from price rather than from cost deflation, and the company specifically attributed what cost inflation there was to ENERGY. That is consistent with the power and carbon risk carried on the input basket. The half captured aluminium reaching four-year highs before the retreat now visible on this board, so it is a backward-looking confirmation of the cycle rather than a forward signal.

earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY WITH A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE. Adjusted net profit Dh2.46bn, up 34% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. The company estimates around Dh1.5bn of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah, most of it in 2026, and guided hot metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 with the smelter currently at about 18% of capacity. THE COMPOSITION IS A PUBLIC CONFIRMATION OF THE MARGIN STRUCTURE THIS BOARD HAS DESCRIBED ALL CYCLE. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. The read-across to the alumina panel is direct - if Alunorte's 50% rate ends up lifting seaborne alumina, this is the margin that compresses first across the Gulf fleet.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

OPERATIONALLY THE WEAKEST PRINT IN THE PEER SET: Q2 net finished production 155,469 t, DOWN 61% y/y, and sales volume 280,799 t, -32% y/y, with Lines 1, 2 and 3 still under controlled shutdown on regional tensions and raw-material availability. Value-added product was 195,891 t, 70% of shipments. THE SHARPEST ILLUSTRATION ON THIS BOARD OF WHAT THE 2026 MARKET IS ACTUALLY REWARDING: a producer can lose 61% of its output year-on-year and still nearly triple half-year profit, because average LME rose 46% y/y to $3,576/t in Q2. It also quantifies the supply loss the deficit rests on - Alba's own read put the Q2 global deficit at 934,000 t including China and 626,000 t excluding it, with global supply contracting about 1% mainly on Middle East disruption. Management explicitly framed the curtailments as preserving flexibility for a swift recovery when conditions improve, which is the restart option the bearish case depends on. Separately Alba is progressing its US$2.2bn acquisition of Aluminium Dunkerque, about 300,000 t/y and the largest EU smelter.

catalysts.text: THE NEXT LME OFFICIAL, AND THE TEST IS RE-SPECIFIED THIS RUN BECAUSE LAST RUN'S WAS MIS-SPECIFIED AND THAT IS ADMITTED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. Yesterday's binary asked for an inventory BUILD or a RESUMED DRAW and got a fourth consecutive reading of exactly zero - a third outcome the test did not allow for. THE RE-SPECIFIED TEST IS THEREFORE THREE-WAY AND THE MOST INFORMATIVE OUTCOME IS THE ONE THAT HAS NOW HAPPENED FOUR TIMES: (a) a FIFTH consecutive zero would establish stasis as the regime rather than a pause, and at that point the flat line stops being news and starts being the baseline; (b) an outright BUILD would confirm the seven-week drawdown has ended and would be the strongest bearish confirmation available; (c) a RESUMED DRAW would mark this week as a pause and would be the best evidence the bull case has had since 11-August. THE SECONDARY QUESTION IS THE SPREAD: a FIFTH consecutive contango, especially another widening one, would make the loose front end a four-session-plus regime rather than an episode; a return to backwardation would be the first genuine sign since 11-August that prompt metal is being competed for. THIRD, THE LEVELS. Cash at $3,227.00 sits $67.50 above the 28-July swing low of $3,159.50, the explicit invalidation carried here. On the upside $3,254.60 - the 38.2% retracement of the whole $3,061.50-to-$3,374.00 advance - is the first level bulls need back and it is only $10.60 away on the three-month.

THE US-CANADA PROCLAMATION, WHICH IS NOW THE SINGLE LARGEST UNRESOLVED POLICY ITEM ON THIS BOARD. The paused escalation deadline of 12:01am Eastern on Saturday 22-August HAS PASSED AND NO PROCLAMATION OR FEDERAL REGISTER NOTICE HAS BEEN PUBLISHED reducing the aluminium rate. The published Section 232 rate on primary aluminium remains 50%. THE PHYSICAL MARKET HAS ALREADY MOVED WITHOUT THE LAW: the September Midwest premium fell 8.2% on 20-August to about $2,094/t with later months down more than 12%. WHAT TO WATCH IS NARROW AND SPECIFIC: whether a proclamation issues at all; whether ALUMINIUM is actually included at 25% rather than only steel; whether derivative products carry a different rate; and whether a quota applies - reporting indicates a quota for steel with aluminium not expected to face one. If the reduction does not materialise, a premium that has already fallen 8.2% on the expectation has room to retrace it.

THE SEPTEMBER PREBAKED ANODE TENDER, NOW CORRECTLY CALENDARED AFTER A CALENDAR ERROR THIS BOARD IS CORRECTING OPENLY. This dashboard had been watching for a print around the 17th-18th of each month and reporting its absence; in fact the Chinese anode tender settles at MONTH-END FOR THE FOLLOWING MONTH. The August settlement therefore printed on 31-July at RMB 5,630/t cash, DOWN RMB 53/t month-on-month, and has been added to the input panel. THE SEPTEMBER PRINT IS DUE AROUND 31-AUGUST AND IT IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL SINGLE INPUT NUMBER ON THIS BOARD, because anodes are roughly 18% of Chinese full cost - the largest consumable after power. THE DIRECTIONAL SETUP IS CONFLICTED AND BOTH SIDES ARE STATED: coal tar pitch, the binder, has risen three consecutive weeks to RMB 4,960/t and feeds anode cost with about a one-cycle lag, which argues for a higher September number; but green petcoke shows a grade divergence with medium and high-sulphur grades softening, which argues the other way.

JACKSON HOLE, AND FED CHAIR KEVIN WARSH'S FIRST APPEARANCE IN THE ROLE. This is a dated macro catalyst and it matters more than usual on this board precisely because of what happened on 21-August: every base metal rose together on a dollar that fell about 0.79% on the week to its lowest since May, with gold up for a fifth consecutive week. A rally driven by the numeraire is hostage to the numeraire. THE PRICED SETUP IS A HIKING RISK, NOT A CUTTING CYCLE, WHICH IS STATED EXPLICITLY BECAUSE IT IS COMMONLY GOT BACKWARDS: CME FedWatch has September at 59.9% unchanged against 40.1% for a 25 basis point HIKE, and October at 45.3% unchanged, 44.9% for a hike and 9.8% for 50 basis points, with the US 10-year at 4.737% approaching a twenty-month high. A hawkish Jackson Hole would reverse the dollar move that produced this week's metals rally; a dovish one would extend it.

MJP Q4-2026 PREMIUM NEGOTIATIONS conventionally open in early September and settle mid-to-late September, against a Q3 settlement of $395/t CIF Japan that is the highest in roughly a decade. A dedicated search this run again returned nothing dated after the 06-July settlement, so the pending quarter is published here as a SCENARIO RANGE of $305-395 rather than as an assessment. THE PUBLIC INPUTS MOVED FURTHER AGAINST SELLERS THIS WEEK. The exchange front end has now printed at or below parity on FIVE consecutive official settlements and the contango re-widened to $17.00, which removes the backwardation exhibit sellers normally lead with. SMM's overseas premium review reports Japanese spot premiums continuing to move lower with cargoes hard to sell and buyers holding bargaining power. And the US Midwest premium falling 8.2% on tariff news establishes a live precedent for regional premiums repricing sharply downward. FOR SELLERS: the Hormuz constraint hardened on an official advisory and ex-China alumina is strengthening, both of which support Asian units.

TWO PEER-EARNINGS GAPS REMAIN OPEN AND THIS DASHBOARD IS PUBLISHING NOTHING FOR EITHER UNTIL A PRIMARY DISCLOSURE LANDS. China's largest producer has still not published its H1-2026 interim - a prior search returned a result set whose internal arithmetic identified it as the H1-2025 interim, and it was rejected rather than used. NO NEW COMPANY WAS BACK-FILLED THIS RUN AND THE REASON IS STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN LEFT AS A SILENT OMISSION: the peer-earnings history now carries fourteen companies covering every name on the priority list, and no verified new quarterly or half-year disclosure printed inside the 20-22 August window that is not already on the board. Back-filling requires a new primary disclosure, not more searching.

A NEW FREE PUBLIC PREMIUM SOURCE MAY BEGIN PUBLISHING, WHICH WOULD MATERIALLY IMPROVE THE WEAKEST PANEL ON THIS BOARD. The LME ran a public consultation, closed 19-August-2026, on launching three new P1020A premium assessments including a DUTY-UNPAID ROTTERDAM series, with intended first publication from 01-September-2026. THREE ROWS ON THE PREMIUM PANEL - European duty unpaid, billets Rotterdam and CIF Japan spot - are currently carried at stale assessment dates precisely because every commercial assessor's number is paywalled, and this board publishes a dated stale figure rather than a guess. An exchange-published, free, dated duty-unpaid series would close at least one of those gaps properly. It is carried as a catalyst rather than an assumption; the consultation closing is not the same as the launch proceeding.

TWO STANDING UNDATED ITEMS, AND THE FIRST IS THE MOST LOAD-BEARING UNVERIFIED CLAIM ON THIS WHOLE PAGE. FIRST: whether the reported claim that ex-China LME aluminium stock is overwhelmingly Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use is ever substantiated or refuted publicly. It is the hypothesis under the reconciliation this board publishes for how an annual global deficit can coexist with a front end that will not pay for prompt metal, and it is carried explicitly as a HYPOTHESIS rather than a fact. Confirmation or refutation would change how every inventory number on this page should be read. SECOND: any change in Hormuz status. That item moved AGAINST reopening this week rather than toward it - threat level SEVERE, zero cargo transits on three consecutive days, and the June memorandum reported to have lapsed around 16-August - so the undated bearish supply event that a reopening would represent looks further away than it did, which is a change worth recording even though nothing was resolved.

risks.text: SUPPLY RELIEF ARRIVES ON A DATED, PUBLISHED SCHEDULE AND CAPS THE RECOVERY - STILL THE DOMINANT RISK ON THIS BOARD AND UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE THIS RUN. No new item was added and none was removed, which is itself worth stating: the schedule does not need refreshing to keep working. It comprises the Gulf smelter at about 18% of 1,262 pots with hot metal guided to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 and its 2.4 Mt/y refinery guided to full technical capability by end-2026; the Australian smelter secured to 2038 on A$2.5bn of government support covering up to 590,000 t/y that had been flagged for possible closure; the largest refinery outside China back at full rate after a three-day gas outage; the Spanish smelter restart completed in April; 75,000 t/y restarting in Slovakia in Q4-2026; a US smelter at full capacity for the first time since 2015; 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium plus 260,000 t/y of CARBON under construction, where the carbon line is the part usually overlooked because anode availability is one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity; and an Indian producer approving further expansion inside a two-phase programme targeting more than 2 Mt. TREND UP, HIGH IMPACT: this is not a forecast, it is a published schedule, and every element of it has a company disclosure behind it.

THE STOCK DRAW HAS STOPPED AND HAS NOW BEEN STOPPED FOR A FULL TRADING WEEK. FULLY MATERIALISED AND HARDENING: LME aluminium warrant has been EXACTLY UNCHANGED at 246,925 tonnes on FOUR consecutive sessions - 18, 19, 20 and 21-August - after 34 consecutive daily declines. YESTERDAY THIS BOARD PUBLISHED A BINARY TEST ASKING FOR EITHER AN OUTRIGHT BUILD OR A RESUMED DRAW AND GOT NEITHER, AND THAT IS REPORTED AS AN UNRESOLVED TEST RATHER THAN SCORED IN ANYONE'S FAVOUR. Four flat prints cannot be attributed to warranting mechanics on any single day; a warrant line that neither builds nor draws across a whole week is describing metal that is neither entering nor leaving the system. THE DISTINCTION THAT KEEPS THIS FROM BEING TERMINAL FOR THE BULL CASE IS BETWEEN LEVEL AND RATE: the absolute level is still a cycle low, with an August average-to-date of 252,678 tonnes against a July average of 282,350, so the LEVEL argument survives while the RATE argument does not. A SUPPORTING DETAIL CUTS THE SAME WAY: cancelled warrants are only about 2,450 tonnes against 244,475 live, a cancellation ratio near 1%, which is not the profile of metal being pulled out. THE COPPER PRECEDENT WEAKENED AS A GUIDE THIS RUN AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED: copper's warrant DREW 1,350 tonnes on 21-August after three builds, and SMM published an analysis attributing copper's move to a short squeeze rather than to supply - so the analogue this board has leaned on all week is less reliable than it looked.

PROLONGED HORMUZ CLOSURE KEEPS GULF SUPPLY IMPAIRED - AND THIS RISK ESCALATED THIS RUN ON PRIMARY, DATED, OFFICIAL EVIDENCE AFTER SEVERAL COMPILES OF BEING CARRIED FLAT. THE TREND IS MOVED FROM FLAT TO UP, AND THE REASON IS SPECIFIC. The UKMTO/JMIC Advisory Update 086 dated 18-August-2026 sets the threat level at SEVERE, stating deliberate hostile action is considered highly likely, and records CARGO VESSEL TRANSITS OF EXACTLY ZERO ON 15, 16 AND 17 AUGUST against a 2025 baseline of roughly 138 vessels per day, with tanker transits of zero, zero and three. It logs 91 confirmed vessel incidents since 01-March-2026, persistent GPS jamming and spoofing, and active drifting-mine risk. Reporting indicates the 17-June-2026 US-Iran memorandum LAPSED around 16-August and that diplomacy has stalled. The region accounted for roughly 10% of global primary production before the conflict. THE PHYSICAL MARKET IS ALREADY PRICING IT INDEPENDENTLY, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST CONFIRMATION AVAILABLE: SMM's 20-August alumina weekly attributes ex-China alumina strength partly to Middle East transport problems lifting bagged-alumina demand, with ex-China alumina now assessed roughly RMB 385/mt above the Chinese index. A reopening remains the single largest bearish supply event available to this market and it remains undated - but the direction of travel this week was away from it, not toward it.

PHYSICAL DEMAND WEAKENS AT THIS PRICE LEVEL. TREND MOVED FROM DOWN BACK TO FLAT THIS RUN, AND THE REVERSAL IS EVIDENCE-LED RATHER THAN A LOSS OF NERVE. For two runs this board moved the trend to DOWN on the strength of consecutive dated sessions showing Chinese ingot physical firming, and that evidence is still valid: SMM's 21-August spot review reports futures stabilising, good warehouse withdrawals, bullish supplier sentiment, East China A00 transactions back to a RMB 10/mt discount-to-premium range from a RMB 40/mt discount two sessions earlier, Central China narrowing to a RMB 40-70/mt discount from RMB 90-120/mt, and regional ingot inventory DOWN 12,000 mt on the day. A NEW AND MATERIAL COUNTER-DATAPOINT ARRIVED THIS RUN AND IT IS WHY THE TREND MOVES BACK: Chinese aluminium BILLET inventory in major consumption areas hit 143,000 tonnes on 20-August, THE HIGHEST FOR THE PERIOD IN FIVE YEARS, up 6,000 tonnes on the prior Thursday, with SMM stating plainly that peak-season restocking HAS FAILED TO MATERIALISE and downstream operating rates are under pressure; cast aluminium alloy social inventory also built for a second consecutive week. THE RECONCILIATION IS THE INSIGHT AND IT IS UNCOMFORTABLE FOR THE BULL CASE: ingot is destocking while BILLET - the first downstream conversion step - is building to a five-year seasonal high. That pattern is consistent with metal moving one step down the chain and stopping, which is a supply-side destock rather than a demand-side one.

POSITIONING UNWIND IN A CROWDED LONG. TREND MOVED FROM FLAT TO DOWN THIS RUN. The configuration that made this risk acute was a fast $312.50 advance into 11-August followed by an accelerating give-back that at one point left the market only $22.50 above its stated invalidation. That configuration has materially improved: the daily losses decelerated (-1.65%, -0.85%, -0.30%) and then REVERSED with a +1.92% session on the forward; the 28-July swing low of $3,159.50 was approached but not tested; and the cushion above it has widened from $22.50 to $67.50. On the Elliott count carried on this board the 20-August low of $3,183.00 sits at a 61.1% retracement of the whole $3,061.50-to-$3,374.00 advance, which is a textbook second-wave depth and a natural place for a corrective sequence to end. THE RISK IS NOT GONE AND THE DOWNGRADE IS DELIBERATELY ONE NOTCH RATHER THAN TWO: a single higher close on a macro session is thin evidence for a completed correction, the front end loosened rather than tightened into it, and a break of $3,159.50 would reopen $3,105 and $3,061.50 quickly.

AN ALUMINA COST SHOCK RE-EMERGES. TREND MOVED FROM DOWN TO FLAT THIS RUN AFTER TEN CONSECUTIVE COMPILES OF DECAYING, AND THE CHANGE IS THE FIRST GENUINE MOVEMENT ON THIS LINE IN THE CYCLE. For ten runs this board argued the alumina threat was fading and that argument was correct: the only credible cost threat of the year, the gas disruption at the largest refinery outside China, resolved in three days, and a second independent source of restoration came online when the Gulf refinery restarted after a 3.5-month shutdown. TWO NEW DATED PUBLIC FACTS NOW CUT THE OTHER WAY AND ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN FILTERED OUT. FIRST, THE EXCHANGE PRICE: LME Alumina closed $363.20/t on 20-August, up 2.23% on the day and up 5.3% from $344.79 on 11-August - a sustained move on a free, settled, dated series rather than an assessment. SECOND, THE DIVERGENCE: SMM's 20-August weekly is headlined that Chinese alumina is drifting lower while ex-China alumina is STRENGTHENING and the spread is widening, with FOB Western Australia at $360/mt implying a China main-port equivalent about RMB 385/mt above the domestic index, and ex-China trades at $409/mt CIF Rotterdam and $400/mt FOB Jamaica. THE REASON THIS IS FLAT AND NOT UP: at $363.20/t against a three-month of $3,244.00 the alumina-to-aluminium ratio is 11.2% against a decade norm of 15-17%, so alumina is still historically cheap relative to metal and the margin cushion is wide. The threat has stopped decaying; it has not become acute.

SMELTER ENERGY AND CARBON COSTS RE-INFLATE - AND THE EVIDENCE GENUINELY SPLIT THIS RUN, WHICH IS A CHANGE FROM THE ONE-DIRECTIONAL STORY THIS BOARD HAS BEEN TELLING. THE TREND IS HELD AT UP BUT THE REASONING IS NARROWER AND IS SET OUT SO IT CAN BE CHECKED. PUSHING COSTS UP: coal tar pitch has risen in each of the last three published SMM weeks to RMB 4,960/t on 13-August, up 1.71% week-on-week and up 5.4% from 23-July, which makes it the clearest live cost inflation on the input panel; silicon rose RMB 200/t week-on-week on expectations of month-end production cuts across 32 Xinjiang furnaces; Brent gained 5.74% on the week to about $94.21 in a second consecutive weekly advance; Chinese thermal coal rose RMB 21/t to RMB 683/t; the August aluminium fluoride tender premium of RMB 250/t is holding rather than fading; and European power costs about 69% more year-on-year on a monthly-average basis. PUSHING COSTS DOWN, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT REQUIRED A CORRECTION: this board wrongly published that the August carbon settlement window closed without a print. IT DID NOT. The Chinese prebaked anode tender settles at MONTH-END FOR THE FOLLOWING MONTH, and the August settlement printed on 31-July at RMB 5,630/t, DOWN RMB 53/t month-on-month. Anodes are the largest consumable after power at roughly 18% of Chinese full cost, so that is the single heaviest line on the panel and it fell. Magnesium also eased RMB 100/t. THE NET IS STILL UP BECAUSE MORE LINES ROSE THAN FELL AND BECAUSE PITCH FEEDS ANODES WITH A ONE-CYCLE LAG, but the margin of the judgement is much finer than it was, and the September anode print around 31-August is now correctly calendared as the test.

A US-CANADA TARIFF AGREEMENT DEFLATES THE US DUTY-PAID PREMIUM - AND THIS RISK STOPPED BEING A RISK AND STARTED BEING A PRICE THIS RUN. IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ITEM ON THIS REGISTER TODAY. The September US Midwest transaction premium was assessed at 95.0 cents/lb on 20-August, about $2,094/t, DOWN 8.2% IN A SINGLE SESSION, with October and November contracts down more than 12% - the market pricing the policy change as biting with a lag. Canada supplies more than half of United States aluminium imports and its H1-2026 shipments to the US were already down 25.03% to 1,039,551 tonnes, with only about 42% of the lost volume re-routed elsewhere. THE HARD-DATED DEADLINE THIS BOARD CARRIED - 12:01am Eastern on Saturday 22-August - HAS NOW PASSED WITH NO PROCLAMATION OR FEDERAL REGISTER NOTICE PUBLISHED, so the legal rate remains 50% and the physical market has repriced an EXPECTATION rather than a law. THE ARITHMETIC ON TWO PUBLIC NUMBERS, AND IT HAS CHANGED SHAPE: at 50% and a $3,227.00 cash settlement the tariff leg is $1,613.50/t, now roughly 77% of the whole $2,094/t premium against about 67% before the fall. The tariff leg did not grow - the MARKET leg collapsed from about $789/t to about $480/t. A premium that is more than three-quarters policy should not be read as a physical-tightness signal. THE OFFSET IS CARRIED: Morgan Stanley's published view is that Canada cannot supply all US demand even at a lower rate, so residual tonnes entering at 50% put a floor under how far the premium can fall.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED BUT THE 19-AUGUST DATA SHARPENS HOW A DEFICIT CAN COEXIST WITH A LOOSENING FRONT END. Refined production outside China has fallen year on year for a second consecutive quarter and output outside China fell 6.7% year on year in July, so the annual deficit is real. Yet LME warrant has now been exactly unchanged on two consecutive sessions and the cash-3M spread has printed a widening contango on both. A deficit is an annual flow concept; a contango is a statement about prompt availability at a specific delivery point. THE RECONCILIATION MOST CONSISTENT WITH THE EVIDENCE, AND IT IS A HYPOTHESIS RATHER THAN A FACT, is that visible ex-China exchange stock is reported to be overwhelmingly Russian-origin material Western buyers cannot use - in which case the exchange series measures something different from accessible Western metal, and a global deficit can coexist with an LME front end that will not pay for prompt delivery. Supporting that reading, the Chinese physical market tightened on 20-August even as the LME curve loosened, with holders withholding and spot quotations firming to a small premium, and SHFE warrants continue to draw at roughly double the LME's monthly rate.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.

caveats: WHICH SESSION THIS BOARD BELONGS TO, STATED FIRST BECAUSE EVERYTHING ELSE DEPENDS ON IT. This run compiled on SATURDAY 22-AUGUST and every LME figure on it is the FRIDAY 21-AUGUST OFFICIAL SETTLEMENT, which is the latest published board. The LME does not trade at weekends, so 21-August is genuinely the most recent session and not a carried one. No intraday or indicative price is presented anywhere as an official.

THE CACHE CROSS-CHECK PASSED FOR A TENTH CONSECUTIVE RUN, AND A HARDER THIRD CHECK WAS ADDED THIS RUN AND ALSO PASSED. The cache-busted German and English Westmetall overviews returned the identical 21-August board, with all six metals, all six stock lines and all three FX fixings rolling together. THE NEW CHECK IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN COMPARATIVE, which makes it far stronger: the August month-to-date cash averages computed independently from the fifteen individual sessions carried on this board reproduce Westmetall's own published monthly-averages pages EXACTLY - aluminium $3,261.80, zinc $3,816.43 and lead $1,850.23 - and that can only happen if every session in every window is correct. Ten clean fetches now stand against four logged cache incidents earlier in the cycle (31-Jul per-metal tables, 04-Aug English overview, 11-Aug per-metal tables, 12-Aug English overview).

TWO CORRECTIONS TO PREVIOUSLY PUBLISHED CONTENT ARE CARRIED THIS RUN AND ARE STATED IN THE OPEN. FIRST, A CALENDAR ERROR: this board repeatedly published that the August carbon settlement window closed without a public print and carried prebaked anodes at July's RMB 5,683/t. The Chinese anode tender in fact settles at MONTH-END FOR THE FOLLOWING MONTH; the August settlement printed on 31-July at RMB 5,630/t, DOWN RMB 53/t month-on-month. SECOND, A FRAMING ERROR: the 15% Section 232 rate available to Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and EU members applies to Annex I-C MOBILE INDUSTRIAL EQUIPMENT ONLY - primary aluminium from all of those origins still pays 50% under Annex I-A.

A PUBLISHED FORWARD TEST WAS MIS-SPECIFIED AND THAT IS ADMITTED RATHER THAN SCORED GENEROUSLY. The prior board asked whether exchange inventory would BUILD or RESUME DRAWING; it did neither for a fourth consecutive session, a third outcome the binary did not allow for. The spread limb of the same test DID resolve cleanly and for the bears - a fourth consecutive contango printed and it re-widened from $1.00 to $17.00. The re-specified test on the next board is three-way.

THE EU IMPORT DUTY OF 6% CARRIED IN THE TARIFF PANEL COULD NOT BE INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED THIS RUN AND THAT IS FLAGGED RATHER THAN LEFT SILENT. TARIC pages returned empty on fetch, and one primary price-reporting source referred to a 3% duty when describing duty-paid versus duty-unpaid Rotterdam economics. The 6% figure is retained because it is the rate this board has carried consistently and the one conventionally used in duty-paid premium arithmetic, but it should be re-verified directly against TARIC or EUR-Lex for CN 7601 10 00 and 7601 20 before being relied upon.

SEVERAL PREMIUM AND INPUT ROWS CARRY OLDER ASSESSMENT DATES BECAUSE THE UNDERLYING ASSESSMENTS ARE PAYWALLED, AND EACH STATES ITS OWN DATE. No figure is published for: the Q4-2026 MJP settlement or negotiation range (the round has not opened publicly); the numeric MJP or CIF Japan spot level (direction is public, the level is not); European duty-unpaid Rotterdam; Rotterdam 6063 billet; FOB Australia alumina (two irreconcilable figures were returned and both rejected); the US Gulf high-sulphur green petcoke 3B quarterly settlement (Argus index fully paywalled); European coal tar pitch; China 99% flake or FOB North-East Asia caustic; any transacted lime price; a China smelter electricity tariff in yuan/kWh; an August-2026 war-risk premium percentage; and August-2026 China PMI, which had not been released.

PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC RATHER THAN CONTINUOUS AND ARE CARRIED AT THEIR PUBLICATION DATES. The MJP Q3 settlement of $395/t is a settled quarterly benchmark from 06-July, not a live assessment. The Q4-2026 figure is published as a SCENARIO RANGE of $305-395 and explicitly not as an assessment, because nothing public has printed inside that round. The tariff-versus-market decomposition IS recomputed every run from the current cash settlement and the published rate.

THE INPUT BASKET CONTAINS NO ESTIMATED, INTERPOLATED OR BASIS-MIXED VALUES. Three rows - smelter electricity, cathode and graphite blocks, and Ti-B grain refiner - carry EMPTY histories by design because no public assessed series exists, and each states that reason. Where a newer series exists on a different basis than the one charted, as with SMM's China green petcoke indices against the Mysteel 3B settlement series on the CPC row, it is reported in text and deliberately excluded from the sparkline. The coal tar pitch row was moved onto the SMM weekly national-average basis this run and that change is disclosed in the row itself.

MODEL BAND, SENTIMENT AND THE FORWARD BLOCK ARE ENGINE-GENERATED FROM THE PUBLISHED DATA AND ARE NOT HAND-AUTHORED. The Elliott Wave section is TECHNICAL CONTEXT ON PUBLIC PRICE DATA AND IS NOT INVESTMENT ADVICE; it carries explicit invalidation levels and probabilities precisely so it can be scored against future boards rather than read as a forecast. Third-party consensus figures, bank forecasts and probability weightings are labelled as such throughout.

EVERYTHING PUBLISHED HERE IS PUBLIC, SOURCED AND GENERIC MARKET INTELLIGENCE. Nothing on this dashboard reflects any company's realised prices, net-backs, shipping lanes, volumes, costs, positions or internal commentary. The only company-specific content is publicly disclosed listed-company information in the peer-earnings and producer-status panels, every row of which cites a public disclosure or press report. Where a number could not be publicly sourced it was not published, and gaps are shown as gaps.

TRADE CORRIDORS ARE REVIEWED MONTHLY OR ON MATERIAL CHANGE RATHER THAN REFRESHED DAILY, AND THIS RUN TRIGGERED A REVIEW RATHER THAN A REWRITE. The Hormuz row was escalated on the 18-August UKMTO/JMIC advisory and the Red Sea position was updated to reflect Suez transits at a two-year high; the underlying corridor map is otherwise unchanged, because churning it daily would obscure genuine regime changes rather than reveal them.
